extracted.intended_audience: aspiring narrative designers and game designers; students and college instructors seeking practical, career-oriented guidance for writing and narrative design in games
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, craft-focused guidance for producing narrative content and narrative design artifacts for digital and analog games, plus portfolio creation and teaching materials for instructors. Emphasizes real-world tasks, industry-ready skills, and classroom assignments/exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative designers' and game designers' day-to-day work
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed look at the work writers and designers perform every day on game development projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use practical descriptions of routine tasks and responsibilities to evaluate or train for the role; emphasizes realistic, production-facing skills rather than abstract theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical advice for breaking into the game industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical advice on how to break into the game industry as a writer or game designer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes career-oriented guidance and insider tips aimed at helping newcomers secure jobs; evaluate career materials by their concreteness and applicability to industry hiring practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio creation and demonstrable narrative design skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers can use the templates and detailed instructions provided here to create lively portfolios that will help open the door to jobs in the game industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolios should include demonstrable narrative design and game design artifacts; the book provides templates and step-by-step instructions—assess portfolio pieces by how well they showcase relevant skills and real-world tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lessons and exercises for skill development
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessons and exercises to help students develop narrative design and game design skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes practice activities; evaluate exercises on clarity, relevance to industry tasks, and ability to build measurable competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching resources: assignments and syllabi
rubrics_metrics.description: A how-to guide for college instructors teaching classes in narrative design and game design. Detailed assignments and syllabi are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For instructors, judge materials by completeness (learning objectives, assignments, templates, schedules) and by alignment with real-world narrative design tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider/AAA development perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: An intimate look at the workings of AAA game development from someone who has spent decades embedded on teams at well-known companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material grounded in AAA production practices should be assessed for relevance to different studio sizes and for actionable takeaways that translate to non-AAA contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story in games
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding 'Story in Games' as a distinct chapter topic—how narrative functions within interactive media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate narrative approaches by how they leverage interactivity, player agency, pacing, and non-linear structures unique to games.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Player’s centrality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Player’s the Thing — prioritizing the player's experience in narrative design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and writing decisions should be evaluated by how they serve player experience, agency, clarity of goals, and emotional engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team collaboration and interdisciplinary work
rubrics_metrics.description: The Team’s the Thing, Too — emphasis on working within development teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative designers must collaborate with designers, programmers, artists; assess work for clear communication, adaptability, and integration with other disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game genres and player expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Game Genres and Their Players — understand different genres and their audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative and design choices should be tailored to genre conventions and player expectations; evaluate fit and appropriateness for target audience and genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: The game development process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Game Development Process — awareness of workflow, milestones, and production realities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative work should align with production phases and constraints; assess deliverables for feasibility, iteration-readiness, and integration into pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing and design for analog games
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing and Design for Analog Games — adapting narrative design principles to non-digital formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate differences in mechanics, physical components, and player interaction when applying narrative techniques outside digital contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: The role of ideas vs execution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Idea Is Everything…and Nothing — perspective on the relationship between concepts and their implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess creative concepts not only for originality but for implementability, scalability, and how well they survive iteration and production constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game development as a craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Game Development as a Craft — treating design and writing as practiced skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize iterative practice, craftsmanship, attention to detail, and continual skill development when evaluating work quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: General writing advice for game writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing Advice — guidance on prose and writing craft as applied to games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standard writing- craft criteria (clarity, economy, voice, pacing) in the context of interactive narrative needs; judge text for player readability and in-game applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career opportunities and job-readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Career Opportunities in the Game Industry — information on roles and pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate career materials by their coverage of role types, required skills, and actionable steps; measure whether guidance helps readers become job-ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials: publications list, syllabi, assignments, templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices include publications list, class syllabi, and course assignments (instructions and templates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ancillary materials should be judged on usefulness, completeness, and ease of adaptation for personal portfolios or classroom use.
